gonna start rewatching some of my fav comfort films cos i cannot for the life of me get myself to lock in on a new movie #depression #nostalgia but ill explore that more in this review guys get ready for another #LOSERREVIEWWWW this is lowk jus another journal entry but dont judge me guys im jus being oppeeennn😛😛😛

like i said before i relate so much to ram , out of all the movies in my literally me tag i think this character is most like me 😭😭😭 (what a LOSER GOSH) but anyway ram lives in the past 24/7, constantly romanticising and idealising his past and i find myself so similar to him in that regard . at the start he goes back to his old school and jus observes everything , going back to all the same spots he did as a kid jus to try and feel the same emotions he did back then yk? just indulging in nostalgia, as if to escape from the present. i find myself going thru all my snap memories , all my saved in chats , my past spam posts even my past logs just to experience all the emotions ive felt before again . i curate memories into museums and write about every significant thing that ever happens to me , i refuse to let my memories disappear yk? i make playlists every month of my fav songs at the time, to bring myself back to the person i was then, to feel the same things and go thru the same memories i did back then. i feel like i have an obsession with immortalising perfect moments so much so that i never fully appreciate the present; the same way ram is so obsessed with photography and freezing moments in time , i feel like i try to capture every good memory i ever have and never let myself live in the moment and cherish it fully; im too scared of losing that memory and losing that evidence that i was happy that day. i just hate having to let go of things yk? 
anyway there’s only one night in the movie where ram doesn’t take his camera out and it’s during his night w jaanu. for the first time he’s no longer trying to preserve and document all his memories but he’s just feeling them. ofc in the end jaanu does end up leaving , and the night does become just a memory but for the first time he was fully present, and maybe the only reason he did that was because he knew this memory would hurt too much to visit. maybe that’s why his suitcase w all his memories of jaanu is tucked and hidden away out of sight, maybe he knew if he’d taken pictures of that night he’d never stop looking at them. 

at the same time, i grieve people before they’ve even left. i miss people who i still talk to everyday , mourning goodbyes before they even happen . maybe that stems from a fear of abandonment from my childhood that i’ve never fully explored idk . i hold onto people like they’re sand; scared of losing people so much so that i forget embrace their warmth whilst i still have them . that scene when they’re on the train and they see the airport rly resonated with me; they’re still together, they’re still enjoying each others presence but ram can feel that inevitable goodbye looming over him and it kinda prevents him from being able to fully cherish what he has whilst he still has it ygm. ok so wtf i try too hard not to forget memories of the past but also think too far forward and both of those things just make me stay zoned out of the current moment what the HELL is my problem😭😭it’s like i’m stuck between two timelines like im in flipping memento or something looool but anyway, i carry the ghosts of ppl who are very much still in my life. maybe thats why i struggle so much to be present w ppl yk, cos a part of me is halfway thru the heartbreak of losing them already. maybe its bc ive had ppl leave my life without warning, maybe its bc ive loved ppl too hard too many times and my brains always preparing for the inevitable ending. the worst part is my friends dont even know that ive alr written the eulogy of our friendship, that ive mourned versions of them that still exist, or that im loosening my grip on people who haven’t even let go yet. when jaanu was sat next to ram n his eyes drifted to the airport, that’s exactly what it feels like for me; grieving in advance, like loving people with a countdown in the background 

i cling to hope to a foolish extent . every connection i create with someone i hold so dearly to my heart , i romanticise my relationship with every person in my life . i still remember when one of my friends was crying to me three weeks ab how she felt she was a burden to everyone in her life, i still remember every time i hug my friends when i say bye to them, i remember every inside joke ive ever made w someone, every emotional intimate convo ive ever had . the same way ram remembers every convo he’s had w his school watchman , i treasure every connection ive ever built with someone . i don’t jus crave connection i yearn for it, and in that yearning sometimes i project more love into people than they know how to accept . and because of that yearning i feel like i overanalyse every mistake i make, n i think the cafe scene was rly relatable in that way. ram and jaanu pretend for a moment that they’re back in the past , rewriting the script for a movie thats alr come out . they replay scenes and change their decisions in hopes of a better outcome , imagining better versions of themselves but in the end nothing changes . i find myself replaying conversations , tweaking dialogues to say better things , hoping i could’ve changed the way things played out , creating a fantasy of what could’ve been . but maybe just like ram im starting to learn that not eeevverryyy story needs to be rewritten , sometimes i just need to take things as they come , feel them once and then let them go 

i wonder what kind of person i’d be if i didn’t remember so much , like if i didn’t write about everything , photograph everything , would i still be me? am i still me without the memories of my past, or am i nothing without those memories? also what am i trying to run away from by not living in the present? am i trying to relive something, protect myself from something, or am i just too scared of what the present demands of me? i guess we’ll never know

Name: Parandhu Po
Review:
time for another #loserreview i needed this movie so bad tn 

very hopeful , chill peaceful movie but there was still a subtle hint of melancholy in it but that was more jus cos i was in a sad mood when i was watching 😭😭

anyway what i really really liked ab this movie was how universal it feels, it’s not a film for kids or for adults or for teenagers it feels like there’s a lesson in it for everyone , i wish id watched this w my family 

i think the big message of this movie tho is to slow down n appreciate the littler things around you yk? i feel like in a similar way to gokul n glory im constantly worried ab the next problem i have to solve, im too busy fighting the future to let myself be fully present . n anbu is like the polar
opposite of that , he takes each moment as it comes n finds beauty in the most ordinary things like a nice sunrise view or feeding the ducks or even just feeling the breeze on his face . he allows himself to wonder , to be lost in the beauty of the world n i think it was a great way of asking the audience, when did we lose our sense of wonder for a sense of control ? i really like how the kid is the ‘guru’ in this movie,  he’s the one we should learn from and not the parents . 

it’s telling us to reconnect w our inner child basically n ive been doing that a loooottt lately , i always say this but im jus indulging in nostalgia yk theres a reason 11 year old rath was so happy with his life he knew what he liked and he stuck with it n now 20 year old rath is going back n exploring the same things , watching the same movies and listening to the same songs and playing the same games (started playing minecraft again what a throwback omg) n i genuinely haven’t felt this content with life in so long . gokul is so locked into a routine at the start of the movie n its only when he goes on that spontaneous road trip , when he lets go of that control over his life, that he rediscovers so much of his past that he’d forgotten , like vanitha . i’ve been reconnecting w a lot of old friends from secondary and even primary school recently and my gooosshhh most wholesome convos of all time this movie couldn’t have come at a better time for me 

i also like how the movie questions our idea of a ‘good life’ . i look back at my happiest moments this past year and i don’t think of when i did well in my uni exams or finally got a job , but i think of those small moments when im with my friends reminiscing about life exploring central london , or even jus laughing ab things sitting in a car park , jus these fleeting moments where i really feel the most alive and happy and im free of all the pressures of things ive yet to achieve . unmaiyaana santhosham isn’t in a 5 year career plan but instead in the unplanned present 

however despite the movie being so jolly n happy n the cute music n all i couldn’t shake this subtle melancholic feeling . not from what was actually happening in the movie but more from the realisation this type of joy where you’re fully free of the routines of urban adult life is temporary yk? the joy of reconnecting w ur younger self is also a reminder of everything that you lost whilst growing up . under all the laughter there’s a quiet sigh when u realise this beautiful journey has to come to an end and the pressures and routine of daily life r just around the corner . everytime i think of those happy moments i mentioned before , i also remember coming back home from those nights n feeling this silence , this emptiness creeping in . its like the sudden absence of all that warmth leaves behind an echo where all that noise and life just was yk? idk how to fully explain what im saying but  the movie gives me a really bittersweet feeling essentially 

anyway loser review OVERRRR bro ts genuinely took me an hour to write i was in my journal SPITTIIINNGGG WOW !!! loved agila ugila superstar’s performance so so much who knew shiva could get me this emotional ?!?!?!? such a cute movie i wish they released this in cinemas in the uk i would’ve been there fdfs 💔 i love these kinda movies that rly make u deep life n i love love loooove writing essay reviews for them ugh somehow this movie escaped my review backlog 🤯🤯 anwyays enna nadanthaalum naan eppothum santhoshama irrupen !! love u guys goodnight 😜

Review:
the fact he still remembered her number after 10 years 💔💔💔  i adore how much manu loved priya man i can’t wait to love a woman like that ! 

i love how realistically the movie handles grief but without glorifying it at allll . i love how they showed that without priya manu is nobody , i think that’s one of the reasons aashiqui resonated so much w me asw yk ? the idea of being so obsessively in love w someone you can’t live without them that’s that realllll yearninnggggg 😝 not healthy at all i know but whateva 

loved the idea of the physical prison vs the mental prison i also like how it parallels with the prison priya was in in side a too , both times they had characters telling them (priya’s mum and prakasha) telling them to escape their mental prisons i thought that was a super cool detail

also love how the themes are contrasting between the films (love and holding on vs grief and moving on) and stylistically it’s contrasting too , side a is lit with diegetic natural lighting , the grading is more desaturated and natural , the flashbacks have this hazy bloom to them whereas in side b all the lighting is artificial and harsh and the grading has this suuuuperr dramatic contrast to it n gosh it’s SOOOOOOO visually gorgeous bro ive said it once n i’ll say it again top 5 most beautiful moves ever ever 

manu aura farming in this movie was soooo satisfying bro the kali subplot HASSS to be my favourite in the entire film the way that entire sequence was lit and especially SCORED and rakshit shetty’s ACTING too it’s all SOOOOO INCREDIBLE !!! again i love how different rakshit plays manu in side A and side B , he goes from this loving sweet caring boy to this violent socially inept reckless man and the transition doesn’t feel jarring at all because behind it all you can see glimpses of side A manu, one of my favourite examples is when he’s fresh out of prison and carrying those mannequins and everyone carries it upright but manu cradles it and stares at its face and priya’s theme plays urrgghhhhhhh i love love looooveee the sound design the cinematography everything bro it all works together SO WELL 

dream sequence was absolutely devastating but so so necessary and EXPERTLY written too i love how the director never writes the ‘easy/satisfying’ way out but he forces you to sit with manu’s discomfort and pain and regret n it makes you that much more immersed in his character . also i never noticed bro the dream starts w the water droplets from the solitary room in side A????? SOUND DESIGGGGNNNNNNN CHAT TO MEEEEE HOW DO YOU EVEN THINK OF THESE IDEAS MANNNNNN . 

theres so much symbolism in the movie too n it would take me 38 rewatches to catch them all (n i wouldnt mind either bro everytime i watch this movie i like it more n more n i cant WAAITTTT to rewatch in 6 months) but anyway one scene i really liked was when surabhi gives him the red hoodie and he wears it over the BLUE shirt its like he’s embracing this new life w a new love new people and all but deep down under that mask he’s still the same old manu w the same everlasting love for priya 

olave olave is one of my favourite songs of all time most defo top 3 , so much so that i downloaded fl studio to make an acoustic bgm version of it 😭😭😭 rath the producer whaaaattt?????? i was slapping heavy reverb on the vocals n panning it n isolating instruments n layering diff parts together n harmonising BRO I WAS COOKINGGG !!! even made a custom casette cover art for it too bro charan raj SHOUT MEEEEE LETS GET BUSSSYYYYYYY

Name: La La Land
Review:
MOVIE NIGHT W NADU MA YEAAAAAHHHHH this was the movie that led to her becoming chellamma so it’s only right we ended up watching it together at some point 

who even was rath before he discovered la la land bro what was my personality before i watched this movie 

i could never begin to describe what this movie makes me feel but the past 2 weeks my life has been in the GUTTER bro like i’ve been happy yes but only because i’ve been completely ignoring anything important to my life all i’ve been doing is calling my friends doomscrolling n playing clash royale , but i got an email today ab my poor attendance n i realised i actually am a uni student bro like i don’t go to a top 5 uni jus to be a bum like my family r lowkey relying on me 😭😭😭 anyway i was having a massive emotional spiral today n i had this feeling that my life was falling apart around me n i just needed something to put my mind at ease n calm my anxiety and as if she could read my mind nadu asked if i wanted to watch la la land . and wow bro . all the fears and worries and all the stress in my mind litr EVAPORAAATEEDDD the second that motorway appeared n another day of sun started playing . bro i was cheesing like i was having the best day of my life i cant put into words how much this movie has healed me during all the lowest points of my life 😭😭😭 for those two hours i wasn’t worried about my poor attendance or living up to the expectations of my family , none of that . i was only worried about mia’s audition and seb’s club and i think it means so much to me how this movie is able to dissolve my reality and replace it with a glimmer of hope , even if it is fleeting . 

i know the movie is all about sacrificing your dreams vs sacrificing your love and even though it is a heartbreaking story , i like how the movie shows there is still hope beyond that sacrifice; mia did end up becoming the star she always wanted to be, seb did open that club he always wanted to. the epilogue is one of my favourite sequences of any movie ever but i think it tells us an important message; you can have your perfect love, or you can live your perfect dream. but you can’t have both! in the dream they did stay together and life did feel like it was in that technicolour world again but the club never came to fruition. and i think seb came to terms with that too, which is why the nod at the end of the film felt less like an “i miss you” and more like a “thank you”. it felt like seb saying “look, i did it”, like he had finally accomplished his dream. i think they both needed each other to get to the place they needed to go; the iconic break up scene at griffith park felt so incredibly mature to me, n i feel like it can be entirely summarised by the line “im always gonna love you” . seb only drives all the to nevada to tell her about the audition because he loves her . mia doesn’t force him to come to paris with her because she loves him . they both know that, despite wanting to be with each other, they will be happier in LA and paris and they have that respect for each other to allow them to fulfill their dreams , yk? they wanted the best for each other, and their love had transformed into something where they allowed themselves to live their perfect dream . 

my entire life and to this day i’ve believed that romantic love is the end all be all, n it’s okay to sacrifice everything to achieve that . but i think the biggest thing this film teaches me is that there’s still hope for a better life even if you don’t prioritise romantic love, because it was only in sacrificing his love for mia that seb was able to make jazz popular again . it was only in sacrificing her love for seb that mia was able to become a famous hollywood actress . i’ve always believed that no relationship whether friendly or romantic becomes a waste of time once it’s over; even if it ended in a bad way that still changed you into the person you are today , n that wisdom n empathy that you gain from that will change the way you see yourself and others in such a beautiful way . 

i could write an essay ab this movie every time i watch it n i can’t wait to write something ab the colour theory of this movie the next time i watch it but woooowwwe man i love la la land . nadu also had this crazy analysis ab the someone in the crown song but cos she takes like a million years to write reviews idk when ill get to read that 💔💔 also BRAV i thought IIIII WAS THE LA LA LAND GUY i thought this was MYYYY movie so imagine the look on my face when i found out nadus watched this movie in TWENNY TWENNY N HAD IT IN HER FAVS BEFORE U EVEN WATCHED IT WTF 😭😭😭anyway i have an exam next week time to lock in aaaaaa but i will fulfill my dreams one day 🤞🏽

anyway love u guys bye

Name: Aftersun
Review:
dear vaanu

how lucky was i,
to feel the pressure of your paws, kneading trust into my skin
to feel the pulse of your heart when you drifted to sleep on my chest
to have my laptop held hostage by your weight on its keys, a quiet protest against my work
to have you wait patiently for treats whilst i’m already late to leave 
to see you run towards me every time i come home
how lucky to see you hide away every time someone new entered the house, only to become your sanctuary when you were afraid
to have to clean up after you every time you used the litter box
to be mad at you every time you threw up on the sofa
to have all my clothes ruined by your thick fur
to have to breathe through allergy pills and sneezes
just to steal one more hour with you by my side

how lucky am i,
to know what it’s like to love and be loved unconditionally 
to be reminded of you in all of my brightest moments, even as you haunt them
to have my eyes turned fragile in your absence
to feel my throat clench when i think of you again
to have you spend your first and last day,
engulfed in the warmth of my bed
you are a fleeting shadow now, a glimpse i catch in the corner of my eye
i have returned you to the soil of the same garden you loved playing in
tucked into the same clothes you made so beautiful with your fur

and how lucky will i be,
to one day show all the love i showed you to a new soul, 
carrying lessons of love only you could teach
to have you gaze over me as i grow older,
learning to grieve and to love through you 
to smile at another and feel your whiskers nudging my memory 
to etch your portrait into my skin, so i don’t have to look far to find you
and to one day meet you again where you rest, walking through the final door to find you running to meet me again 

two years was never going to be enough, 
but you were so small, and yet you left the biggest hole in my heart 

you’re resting peacefully in eternity now
but you’re still here, 
embroidered in all the shirts i own,
woven in the very way i breathe

Name: Highway
Review: nadu kutty you never miss w your movie recs  this was such an incredibly heavy film i went into it expecting a bog standard stockholm syndrome story but came out with TEARS in my eyes FACK 💔 veera  from the start of the movie we get a clear picture of who veera is; she’s a woman who cherishes freedom and adventure, and is in a position in life with a wealthy family and big house where she’s able to act on that freedom more than the average person. she’s due to marry a man who clearly doesn’t share the same views as her; vinay prioritises ‘tradition’ and ‘reputation’, he’s very conservative. he doesn’t even wanna go for a late night drive with veera, n only after she nags him does he finally give in . when she gets kidnapped at the petrol station, we watch as all her freedom is stripped away from her, as she’s pulled away from the safety of her home.  however as the movie progresses, and the cinematography shifts to wide shots of open nature, and the colours shift to more earthy, vibrant tones, we begin to realise that veera was not kidnapped, but ironically she was freed. she’s been carrying the weight off being sexually assaulted as a child for over a decade, and the person who was supposed to be her shield from it all, her own mother, shunned her for confiding in her. just like her fiance vinay she prioritised the family image and reputation over the safety and wellbeing of her own daughter.  when veera is finally outside, we begin to see a change in her demeanour. she’s moved away from the home where she has to perform as this perfect rich daughter, n is finally free in nature to express her pain.  mahabir even more so than veera this feels like a character study of mahabir. he’s introduced as the villain of the film, a man completely swallowed by his environment, carrying a heavy, ruthless and almost suffocating energy. he’s haunted by his past, believing that the murders he committed have permanently stained his soul. “two men die with one bullet, the one who’s shot and the one who shoots”. to mahabir, the humanity within him died when he pulled that trigger 20 years ago he’s convinced himself he’s a monster entirely unworthy of love or even kindness. the few times he looks at veera, he has this cold glare that makes it seem like he isn’t quite fully present. he grew up thinking he’s unlovable n undeserving of forgiveness, n so he protects himself with violence and fear. it seems like he spends his entire adulthood running away from the memory of being an adored son, to the point he thinks he’s too far gone to ever be loved again  healing the meat of the story is in the dynamic between the two. at the core both characters are unseen by the rest of the world, which is the foundation on which their entire relationship is built.  one of the most significant scenes is when mahabir listens to veera’s SA story. unlike her family who treated her truth like a stain on their reputation, mahabir just listens. he doesn’t judge her or try to fix her, he doesn’t even look away. he becomes a silent witness n allows her to be broken in front of him, and from experience i know how relieving having someone like that can be. her pain wasn’t a burden to mahabir, instead she was finally seen by him. that’s why she feels so safe around him, she isn’t seen as a monster for having that story, she’s seen as human. it’s the moment where mahabir shifts from the villain of the story to, in a way, the hero.  as veera slowly heals, she turns that same empathetic lens onto mahabir, and it’s so beautiful yet painful to watch his facade crumble. he’s spent so long building this wall of violence and fear to protect himself from his memories, but veera’s the first person who peered past that into his soul. she doesn’t see the monster he thinks of himself as, she sees the boy who misses his mother. my favourite scene of the entire movie is near the end when they find that house in the mountains. she cooks him food and puts a pottu on, she’s offering him love. he sees a version of his life he thought was forever removed from his future, and it breaks him. he can handle being hated or feared, he can handle being hunted, but he cannot handle being adored. he runs out the house to wash his face, trying to steady his breath in the nature he often found solace in, but he also begins to realise he wants this. he yearns for that forgiveness, that love, that gentleness that he’s been starved of for two long decades.  he tries to fight off veera’s comfort at first, convincing himself that this love can never be his, he cries for his mother, he breaks down completely. but veera’s persistence, her unconditional love shrinks him back down into that adored son, and he can no longer fight himself. veera accepts him as the broken man he is, and still offers him love. mahabir saw her as the broken woman she was, and still offered her love. they both gave each other the permission to be free and be forgiven.  being set free the ending isn’t happy in the traditional sense, but it’s the only one that makes sense for a story this heavy. mahabir gave veera the strength to find her voice, and veera gave mahabir the strength to finally accept love, and accept himself. so when he’s murdered, in a way there’s happiness in knowing he died finally having an ounce of love for himself. in a way, veera too is finally set free. when she goes back home, she stands in front of her ‘respectable’ family n exposes her uncle in front of everyone. she let go of that version of herself that lived in fear, she’s finally free. and in the final shot, we see her in her safe space, the mountains.  the mountains this movie was sooo difficult to get through cos to an extent i saw myself in mahabir. i spent so much of my life convincing myself i was unworthy of love, for so long that it didn’t feel like i was trying to persuade myself anymore. i fully embodied that mindset and i let it dictate so much of my life. i rejected so much affection, believing i wasn’t deserving of it, even though deep down it was what i craved more than anything. when i tell people my own SA story i riddle it with jokes to make it seem less serious, because i wasn’t worthy of being pitied. i was so afraid of being a burden that id hide my pain behind this unserious persona, even thought all i’ve ever craved was that gentleness.  it’s why seeing mahabir break down made me cry too. when you live in that darkness for so long, the light doesn’t feel warm, it feels like it’s burning you. watching veera offer him love not because he was good to her, but just because he’s a person and inherently deserving of it, it made me realise that his struggle to accept love was because he was so terrified of being seen for the real him. he was terrified of being seen as vulnerable. maybe i’ve been running from the same thing. seeing him finally find peace in her comfort gave me a bit of hope that i don’t have to keep pushing myself away from what i want either.  nadu my chellamma thank u so much for forcing me to watch this movie i will never forget the things it made me feel. almost teared up writing this stupid review asw bra fuck this movie 😭😭😭
